questions.visual_target: Given this immunostain panel, which lineage is most likely and which site should be evaluated for a primary tumor?
questions.stem: Given this immunostain panel, which lineage is most likely and which site should be evaluated for a primary tumor?
options: Mesothelial lineage; evaluate the pleura.
Colorectal epithelial lineage; evaluate the colon.
Pulmonary epithelial lineage; evaluate the lung.
Renal epithelial lineage; evaluate the kidneys.
Müllerian epithelial lineage; evaluate the adnexa.
choice_rationales: Calretinin is negative, so the panel offers less support for mesothelial lineage. The combined positive pattern favors Müllerian epithelium. This choice describes mesothelioma.
CDX2 is negative, weakening the colorectal alternative. The positive PAX8 and CA125 pattern fits the Müllerian workup. This choice describes colorectal adenocarcinoma.
TTF1 is negative, and the combined panel fits Müllerian origin better than a pulmonary primary. Pleural fluid is the sampling site. This choice describes lung adenocarcinoma.

PAX8 can occur in renal as well as Müllerian tissue. PAX8 alone cannot establish renal origin, and the other positive markers and follow-up favor the adnexa. This choice describes renal cell carcinoma.

CK7, PAX8 and CA125 positivity together favor Müllerian lineage, prompting evaluation of the adnexa. This choice describes a Müllerian (ovarian or tubal serous) carcinoma, which is what the image shows.
questions.explanation: Immunostains narrow lineage before they identify a precise anatomic primary. In this case the panel supported Müllerian carcinoma and ovarian follow-up established the primary. PAX8 alone would not distinguish an ovarian source from a renal or other PAX8-positive source.
visual_clues: CK7, PAX8, and CA125 are positive.

questions.lead_in: Which change is visible on the exposed cervical surface?
questions.condition_overview: Trichomonas vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan sexually transmitted infection causing frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge, vulvovaginal itching, dysuria, and a strawberry cervix with punctate hemorrhages, with vaginal pH above 4.5. Wet mount shows motile pear-shaped trophozoites with flagella, and the Pap smear can show pear-shaped organisms. Perinuclear halos in squamous cells can mimic it but are a pseudoparasite. Treatment with metronidazole should include partners.

questions.lead_in: At four months since the last period, which statement about the two milestones applies to the case?
questions.condition_overview: Menopause is the permanent end of menstruation after 12 months of amenorrhea, at an average age of about 51, caused by depletion of ovarian follicles. Estradiol and inhibin B fall, so FSH (and later LH) rise, and the main estrogen becomes extragonadal estrone from adipose aromatization of androstenedione. Estrogen deficiency causes hot flashes, vaginal atrophy, sleep disturbance, bone loss and osteoporosis, and adverse lipid changes. Perimenopause is the preceding transition with irregular cycles, and treatment is symptomatic, including hormone therapy in selected patients.

questions.condition_overview: Menopause is the permanent end of menstruation after 12 months of amenorrhea, at an average age of about 51, caused by depletion of ovarian follicles. Estradiol and inhibin B fall, so FSH (and later LH) rise, and the main estrogen becomes extragonadal estrone from adipose aromatization of androstenedione. Estrogen deficiency causes hot flashes, vaginal atrophy, sleep disturbance, bone loss and osteoporosis, and adverse lipid changes. Perimenopause is the preceding transition with irregular cycles, and treatment is symptomatic, including hormone therapy in selected patients.

questions.condition_overview: In hypergonadotropic hypogonadism (primary), the gonads fail despite adequate pituitary drive, so loss of negative feedback from estradiol, testosterone, and inhibin raises FSH and LH. questions.condition_overview: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) is HPV-driven dysplasia of the cervical squamous epithelium graded by the depth of epithelium replaced by atypical cells (CIN 1 lower third, CIN 2 two thirds, CIN 3 full thickness). Higher grades are treated by excision or ablation to prevent invasive carcinoma.

questions.condition_overview: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) are benign smooth muscle tumors and the most common tumor in women, growth being estrogen and progesterone dependent. They are classified as submucosal (beneath the endometrium, causing the most bleeding), intramural (within the wall), or subserosal (beneath the serosa, causing pressure effects). They are well-circumscribed, firm, whorled, white-tan masses with interlacing bundles of uniform spindle cells without atypia. Symptoms include heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pressure, and infertility, and they shrink after menopause. Malignant transformation (leiomyosarcoma) is rare.

questions.condition_overview: Seminoma is the most common testicular germ cell tumor, in men aged 15 to 45. It forms a homogeneous, pale tan-white, fleshy, bulging mass. questions.condition_overview: Testicular torsion is twisting of the spermatic cord that cuts off venous and then arterial blood flow, causing sudden severe scrotal pain, a high-riding testis, and absent cremasteric reflex. It most often affects adolescents with a bell-clapper deformity. Doppler ultrasound shows reduced or absent perfusion on the affected side. Untreated torsion leads to hemorrhagic infarction (dark, swollen testis with coagulative necrosis), and salvage requires surgery within about 6 hours.

questions.condition_overview: Endometriosis is the presence of functional endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterus, most often on the ovaries, pelvic peritoneum, and rectovaginal septum, and rarely in the bladder, vagina, or even the lung. Ectopic tissue responds to cyclic hormones, bleeds, and causes chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Patients have dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, dyspareunia, and infertility. Ovarian involvement forms endometriomas (chocolate cysts) filled with old blood. Microscopically two of three elements are needed: endometrial glands, stroma, and hemosiderin-laden macrophages. Catamenial symptoms, such as thoracic or bladder symptoms with menses, suggest distant implants.

questions.condition_overview: Adenomyosis is the presence of benign endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium, deeper than the usual endometrial-myometrial junction. The uterus enlarges symmetrically and has a thickened, trabeculated wall with small cystic or hemorrhagic foci. Patients have heavy, painful menses and a boggy, tender uterus. Microscopically there are islands of endometrial-type glands with stromal cuffs among smooth muscle bundles, with hypertrophy of the surrounding muscle. On MRI it thickens the junctional zone. Definitive treatment is hysterectomy.

questions.stem: Where does the lecture direct attention for a uterine-wall component of the symptoms?
options: Within a periurethral outpouching below the bladder.
Only within the fluid of a dominant ovarian follicle.
At a feeding stalk projecting into a saline-distended cavity.
At the wall of the rectum, without uterine involvement.
At the junction of endometrium and myometrium, within the uterine wall.
choice_rationales: A periurethral diverticulum lies below the bladder near the urethra. Adenomyosis alters the junctional zone within the uterine wall. This choice describes a periurethral outpouching.
A dominant follicle is ovarian. The inner myometrial change shown here is within the uterine wall, supporting adenomyosis. This choice describes the fluid of an ovarian follicle.

The separate endometrial polyp example shows a stalk in the uterine cavity. The adenomyosis view focuses on the inner myometrium at the junctional zone. This choice describes a feeding stalk in a distended cavity.
The indicated change relates to the endometrial–myometrial interface. This choice describes the rectal wall.

The adenomyosis finding is at the endometrial–myometrial junction inside the uterine wall. The endometrioma is the separate adnexal finding. This choice describes adenomyosis (the junction of the endometrium and myometrium), which is what the image shows.
questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts the adnexal lesion with abnormality of the inner myometrium at the junctional zone. These images illustrate why the uterine and adnexal findings are assessed separately.
visual_clues: On both views use the endometrium to locate the inner myometrium.

Microscopically there are islands of endometrial-type glands with stromal cuffs among smooth muscle bundles, with hypertrophy of the surrounding muscle. On MRI it thickens the junctional zone. Definitive treatment is hysterectomy.
